vo_text.1: Why do most anglers never land a ten pound bass? Because you're fishing where small fish live.
vo_text.2: Double-digit record largemouth aren't just bigger. They're a completely different animal. They rarely roam shallow banks. Instead, they lock onto deep primary structure: steep drop-offs, river channel bends, and submerged timber in fifteen to thirty feet of water.
vo_text.3: To trigger a world-class female, stop throwing small baits. Giant bass feed on high-calorie prey like rainbow trout, gizzard shad, or bluegill. Throw eight to ten inch magnum swimbaits or heavy glide baits, fished ultra-slow right in their strike zone.
vo_text.4: When she strikes, it's not a tap. It's a heavy suction. Heavy-power rods and twenty pound fluorocarbon are non-negotiable if you want to turn her head.
vo_text.5: Go big, fish deep, and hit subscribe for more trophy breakdown guides.
